w:r.w:t: Deploying the Same ServiceNow SDK Application to Any New Instance
Step-by-step runbook for build, OAuth authentication, company-key trust, installation, verification, and troubleshooting

For a new target instance, do NOT run now-sdk init again and do NOT generate a new scopeId. The same application identity (scope + scopeId) is reused on every target instance. Only the target-instance authentication and trust configuration change.
1. What You Do for Every New Instance
Confirm the local project and now.config.json are unchanged.
Create an OAuth credential alias for the new ServiceNow instance.
On the target instance, make sure company key 2002152 is trusted in sn_appauthor.all_company_keys.
Build the project with the local SDK.
Install the package to the new instance using that instance's alias.
Verify the application record and 48/48 flow activation.
For later source changes, build once and install to each target alias.
Do not clone the application identity
Keep now.config.json with scope x_2002152_nwforge and scopeId 293d4f8e3d324ec58f5be29136f38fe5. Changing either value creates an identity mismatch and can break upgrades.
2. Values to Know Before You Start
Use a Node.js version supported by the project dependencies; an LTS release is preferred for repeatable tooling.
Run commands from the project workspace, not from C:\Windows\System32 or another folder.
Use the project-local ServiceNow SDK version from package.json. For this project it is 4.12.2.
You need an administrator-capable account on the target instance for OAuth authorization and required instance configuration.
4. Confirm the Application Identity (Do This Once)
The file should contain the same identity on every machine and for every target instance:
Do not replace the scopeId with a new value for QA/UAT/Prod or another PDI. scopeId is the application identity, not the instance identity.
5. Add OAuth Authentication for the New Instance
Choose a short alias that identifies the target, for example
npx now-sdk auth --add https://dev181876.service-now.com --type oauth --alias dev
The SDK opens the target instance in your browser.
Log in normally to the target instance.
On the ServiceNow SDK consent screen, select Allow.
Copy the short-lived OAuth code from the browser and paste it only into the terminal prompt.
Never put a ServiceNow password in a URL, script, document, or chat. Never share OAuth authorization codes. If a password or code is exposed, rotate/reset it and start a fresh OAuth flow.
6. Prepare the New Instance to Trust This App Scope
. A new instance may have a different local company code, so it must explicitly trust 2002152 for this application.
Do not change the target company code
Do not overwrite glide.appcreator.company.code. Keep the target instance's own code and append 2002152 only to sn_appauthor.all_company_keys.
Open the target instance and navigate to sys_properties.list.
Open glide.appcreator.company.code and note the current value. Do not modify it.
Preserve every existing value and append 2002152 as a comma-separated key.
Save/Update the property and allow the property cache flush to complete.
If the property is not editable on a PDI, an administrator can use Scripts - Background (Global) with this safe append-only script:
var updated = current ? current + ',' + KEY : KEY;
On enterprise, production, or tightly governed instances, coordinate this trust change with the ServiceNow platform owner or support process. Do not bypass organizational change controls.
If the source has not changed
You do not need to rebuild before every repeat install. Build after source changes; then install that build to each prepared target instance.
A successful install should end with messages similar to:
[now-sdk] Installation completed. Access the application at: https://<INSTANCE>.service-now.com/sys_app.do?sys_id=293d4f8e3d324ec58f5be29136f38fe5
Do not use --reinstall for normal updates

--reinstall can remove server-side metadata that is not represented in the local package. Use the normal install/update flow unless you intentionally need a destructive reinstall and understand the impact.
Open the application URL printed by the SDK.
Confirm the application record sys_id is 293d4f8e3d324ec58f5be29136f38fe5.
Confirm the terminal reports Flow activation complete: 48/48 succeeded.
If needed, run npx now-sdk install --info --auth <ALIAS> and open Upgrade History.
10. Deploying the Same Build to Multiple Instances
Prepare a separate OAuth alias for each target. Example:
OAuth credentials and the company-key trust must be set up separately on each new target. After that, future updates are normally just build + install to the desired alias.
OAuth opens https://dev.service-now.com instead of your PDI
The target URL was not supplied correctly. Cancel and run: npx now-sdk auth --add https://<real-instance>.service-now.com --type oauth --alias <alias>.
now.config.json is missing or invalid. Restore the fixed application identity shown in Section 4.
Unable to install application as application was null

First verify sn_appauthor.all_company_keys contains 2002152. Then check the failed sys_execution_tracker record, Upgrade History, and the ServiceNow IDE/server-side SDK support on the target instance.
Access Token has expired, refreshing token
Normal. The SDK can refresh the OAuth token automatically; wait for the install to continue.
Install appears stuck at a high percentage
Do not immediately press Ctrl+C. PDIs can be slow. Wait, then inspect Upgrade History / Execution Tracker if it does not finish.
Inspect the named Fluent source. A subflow must contain at least one Action Instance. In this project, Resolve Approval Matrix already has a minimal log action and should activate successfully.
PowerShell says Set-Location positional parameter / command not recognized
Two commands were pasted together. Run cd and npx/npm commands on separate lines.
npm audit reports SDK transitive vulnerabilities
Do not run npm audit fix --force blindly. It can downgrade/change the SDK. Keep the project SDK pinned and review fixes intentionally.
Use the organization's admin/support process. Do not change the app scope or company code just to bypass the control.
Project now.config.json still uses scope x_2002152_nwforge and the original scopeId.
Target URL is known and reachable.
New OAuth alias created and visible in npx now-sdk auth --list.
Target sn_appauthor.all_company_keys contains 2002152 while preserving existing keys.
npm run build completed successfully after the latest source changes.
NowForge Flows application record opens and shows the correct scope.
No passwords or OAuth codes were stored in scripts, URLs, screenshots, or documentation.
